title: Human Cell
summary: Explore the microscopic anatomy of the human cell, including the nucleus, mitochondria, and cell membrane.
focus: Cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria (ATP), endoplasmic reticulum, and ribosomes.

cues.text: Welcome to this demo class from Qrie AI! Every human cell is enclosed by a flexible, selective cell membrane.
Inside lies the nutrient-rich cytoplasm, a protective jelly suspending every vital organelle in a fibrous network.
Notice our dynamic, rounded human cell shape on the board, built for natural flexibility across our living tissues.
At the center sits the nucleus, the master control library storing all your genetic DNA instructions safely inside nuclear pores.
Surrounding the nucleus are oval mitochondria, the renowned powerhouses of the cell that generate life-giving ATP energy from oxygen and glucose.
Notice the inner folded cristae maximizing surface area for chemical reactions, powering hardworking tissues like heart and muscle cells every millisecond.
Look at the folded ribbon channels wrapping the nucleus. Which cellular organelle synthesizes new proteins from genetic instructions?
Pause here to trace these folded membranes and consider how organelles collaborate.
Those tiny specks are ribosomes, and the surrounding highway is the rough endoplasmic reticulum, busily assembling amino acid chains into functional proteins.
The Golgi apparatus packages and addresses these finished proteins into vesicles for delivery, completing the essential cellular manufacturing and shipping line.
All these specialized organelle systems coordinate harmoniously, sustaining life across trillions of human cells.
From firing neurons to contracting muscles, cellular teamwork makes complex human function possible every single day.
That concludes this demo class from Qrie AI! Review your notes and questions, and I will see you next time!

notes.title: The nucleus commands and protects DNA
notes.text: The nucleus is enclosed by a double-layered nuclear envelope with pores regulating transport. Inside, DNA stores the master genetic blueprint for synthesizing all proteins required by the human body.

notes.title: Mitochondria generate cellular fuel
notes.text: Through cellular respiration, mitochondria break down glucose in the presence of oxygen to synthesize adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy currency utilized across all cellular metabolic processes.

notes.title: Protein production pipeline: Ribosomes to Golgi
notes.text: Ribosomes bound to the rough endoplasmic reticulum assemble amino acid chains. The synthesized proteins travel to the Golgi apparatus, where they undergo folding, biochemical modification, and vesicular packaging.

mistake: Human cells possess flexible cell membranes and active mitochondria to support dynamic physiological functions across diverse human tissues.

practice.question: Why do active muscle cells contain substantially higher concentrations of mitochondria than skin cells?
practice.answer: Muscle cells continuously contract and require high quantities of ATP energy, which mitochondria produce via aerobic cellular respiration to power muscular exertion.
